prior_passes.notes: No source found naming a distinct 6.1 km 'SUMED Gas Pipeline' with its own endpoints. Corridor hypothesis only: GASCO (engineering/PM) and Petrojet (construction) built marine and onshore pipelines at SUMED Port, Ain Sokhna to carry regasified LNG from the FSRU marine berth into the national gas grid (Egyptian Gazette, Daily News Egypt) — P8005 is plausibly the short onshore continuation of P8004's offshore leg (SUMED terminal landfall to a national-grid tie-in point a few km inland), but no source states a distinct length, a named tie-in facility, or its own coordinate. Recommend a follow-up pass with fresh search budget: Egypt Oil & Gas / Enterprise Press archives, GASCO project pages, or Arabic search ('خط أنابيب سوميد للغاز', 'الشبكة القومية') targeting the onshore segment specifically.

start.name: SUMED Pipelines Terminal (Ain Sokhna / Ain Sukhna port)
start.coord_basis: Centroid of an OSM landuse=industrial polygon explicitly named 'SUMED Pipelines Terminal' / 'محطة نهائية لأنابيب سوميد' (source tag: Bing import), queried directly via the Overpass API (bbox search around Ain Sokhna, since Nominatim's public search returned no hits for 'SUMED' + Ain Sokhna). Corroborated as SUMED's Ain Sokhna facility (hosts the 'Ain Sukhna Product Hub' FSRU/regasification operations) by sumed.org and by the Egyptian Maritime Transport Authority's port page (SUMED port sits south of Ain Sokhna port on the Suez Gulf's western shore).

prior_passes.notes: Partially advanced but still unresolved: confirmed via multiple independent press sources (egyptoil-gas x2, al-khaber, dailynewsegypt) that GASCO (materials/engineering) and Petrojet (construction), with Enppi, are laying 'onshore and offshore gas pipelines of various lengths and large diameters' plus loading arms at SUMED's Ain Sokhna berth to carry regasified LNG from FSRUs 'into the national grid' -- this matches the prior pass's corridor hypothesis and rules out the 320km SUMED oil corridor (Ain Sokhna-Sidi Kerir) as the identity: no source ties a gas line to Sidi Kerir, all describe a short onshore tie-in near the berth, consistent with the sheet's implied short length. Got a solid, independently-sourced START this pass: the named 'SUMED Pipelines Terminal' facility itself (OSM-tagged industrial site + corroborating SUMED/port-authority sources), which anchors the marine/FSRU end of the line. STILL MISSING: no source names a specific tie-in facility for the onshore end -- articles only say gas is injected 'into the national grid' without naming a station. One same-day-reported GASCO facility, the 'National Gas Control Center (NATA)', came up in searches (Madbouly's Ain Sokhna visit continued to a NATA tour per an Egypt Oil & Gas piece) but the source explicitly does NOT state NATA is this pipeline's terminus or give NATA's location, so using it would be inference, not sourcing -- excluded per standing rule 2. Checked Overpass/OSM for a distinctly-named onshore gas line near the SUMED terminal: found only an unlabeled man_made=pipeline/substance=gas way starting ~4km from the SUMED terminal and running ~60km inland toward Cairo -- too long to be this line and untagged with any project name, so also excluded (using an unlabeled OSM way's endpoint would be fabricating an identity, not geocoding a named place). Recommend a follow-up targeting GASCO/Petrojet project-specific documentation (contract award notices, EGAS annual report) or Arabic trade press for the SUMED-berth line specifically, distinguishing it from the separately-documented 36-inch/17km Sonker Port line (a different, nearby berth's pipeline -- not this PID).

start.name: Sonker Bulk Liquids Terminal, Basin 3, Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Wikipedia coordinate for Ain Sokhna port/town (29°36'00"N 32°19'00"E) — general port-area location only; Sonker's Basin 3 terminal sits within Ain Sokhna/Sokhna Port but no more precise public coordinate was found for the jetty itself

prior_passes.notes: Sonker (Sonker Bunkering Company / Sonker Energy) operates the Bulk Liquids Terminal at Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Gulf of Suez — a site that berths FSRUs and feeds regasified LNG into Egypt's national gas grid via dedicated pipelines built 'outside the port fence' (IFC ESRS disclosure, re: an adjacent line as an analogue). Two FSRUs began operating from Sonker in 2015 -- Hoegh Gallant (March, 500 MMSCFD) and BW Singapore (November, 750 MMSCFD) (Sonker company history page) -- a plausible basis for GEM's 'Phase 1'/'Phase 2' gas-line split (one grid tie-in per FSRU), but no source names which phase is 9 km vs 7 km, nor identifies the specific national-grid valve/metering station each ties into. A separate, later (2025) GASCO/Petrojet gas-import pipeline (17 km, 36-inch, 3 valve rooms, built by Petrojet) for a third FSRU at Sonker is documented in the two Daily News Egypt articles -- that is a newer, distinct project, not P8006/P8007. Could not source a specific end-point name/coordinate for either phase this session (WebSearch budget exhausted mid-task, shared across concurrent research). Recommend a follow-up pass targeting GASCO's network map / EIA filings to pin the tie-in point, and to determine which phase is 9 km vs 7 km.

start.name: Sonker Bulk Liquids Terminal, Basin 3, Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Wikipedia coordinate for Ain Sokhna port/town (29°36'00"N 32°19'00"E) -- general port-area location only; Sonker's Basin 3 terminal sits within Ain Sokhna/Sokhna Port but no more precise public coordinate was found for the jetty itself

prior_passes.notes: RETRY -- still unresolved on the delivery end. Dedicated second-pass research (WebFetch against IFC's full ESRS disclosure text, GASCO's own gas-grid page, EGAS/EGPC/petroleum.gov.eg press coverage, and Egypt Oil & Gas trade press; WebSearch was unavailable, session-wide quota exhausted) found no public source naming a specific downstream valve/metering/compressor station or power plant for either Sonker gas pipeline phase. The IFC ESRS document (project 36828, covering the FIRST FSRU era, i.e. Hoegh Gallant/2015) states plainly that 'the natural gas is compressed to approximately 80 bar and delivered through loading arms installed on the jetty into the national grid for distribution' -- with NO named station -- and separately identifies EGAS (not GASCO) as the pipeline operator ('the pipelines by EGAS'). GASCO's own gas-grid page (gasco.com.eg -- fetched via proxy since direct WebFetch/url_verifier both fail on the site's SSL cert, so this URL is NOT included in route_refs per the hard rule to drop failing URLs) names only its Dahshour compressor station and a Suez SCADA control center -- nothing Ain Sokhna-specific. The IFC document also names 'Mina Sadat' (Sadat Port/Terminal, EPROM's crude single-buoy-mooring terminal at Ain Sokhna km-30) as a grid tie-in point, but explicitly for the SEPARATE 37.5 km GASOIL/diesel pipeline at the same site, not the gas line -- using it here would not be defensible, so it is deliberately NOT used as this endpoint. The 2025 GASCO/Petrojet 36-inch/17km pipeline covered in the two Daily News Egypt articles remains confirmed as a later, distinct project for a THIRD FSRU, unrelated to P8006/P8007. The Hoegh Gallant (Mar 2015) vs. BW Singapore (Nov 2015) FSRU-to-phase mapping also remains an unconfirmed inference (Sonker's own history page never uses 'Phase 1'/'Phase 2' language). MISSING: a named, geocodable delivery-end facility distinct from 'the national grid' in general. Next step would need an EGAS annual report or an Arabic-language GASCO network-map PDF, neither locatable via WebFetch alone this session.
